title: How Netanyahu is capitalizing on MBZ meeting, FlyDubai attack to gain in election polls
gist: With four weeks to Israel's Oct. 27, 2026 election, Mazal Mualem reports that security — boosted by Netanyahu's MBZ meeting and the Sept. 30 alleged FlyDubai hijacking attempt — has displaced ultra-Orthodox draft issues as the central campaign theme, narrowing the bloc gap: a Maariv poll put Netanyahu's coalition at 51 seats (+2) versus 53 (-2) for the Zionist opposition and 12 for Arab parties.

themes.theme: Security shift in Israel's election campaign

insights.claim: With four weeks before Israel's Oct. 27 elections, security is re-emerging as the central campaign issue, a shift Israeli political sources say could benefit Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
insights.speaker: Mazal Mualem
insights.so_what: Raises the probability of Netanyahu retaining power, implying continuity in Israel's regional security posture.
insights.quote: security is once again emerging as a central campaign issue in a shift that Israeli political sources say could benefit Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
insights.locator: JERUSALEM — With four weeks to go

insights.claim: The campaign had previously focused on ultra-Orthodox military service and funding for ultra-Orthodox institutions; current security threats help explain the narrowing gap between the political blocs.
insights.speaker: Mazal Mualem
insights.so_what: Issue salience is moving away from Netanyahu's coalition's weak point toward its traditional strength.
insights.locator: After the campaign had focused on ultra-Orthodox

insights.claim: A Maariv poll published Oct. 2 showed Netanyahu's coalition gaining two seats to 51, the Zionist opposition bloc losing two to 53, and Arab parties at 12 Knesset seats.
insights.speaker: Mazal Mualem
insights.so_what: Neither bloc reaches a 61-seat majority, so Arab parties and coalition arithmetic remain decisive for the post-election government.
insights.quote: showed Netanyahu's coalition gaining two seats this week, bringing its total to 51

insights.claim: In the same poll, Likud rose to 19 seats from 18, while Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar slipped to 21 from 22, remaining the largest single party.
insights.speaker: Mazal Mualem
insights.so_what: Eisenkot's party leads but momentum is shifting toward Likud.

themes.theme: Netanyahu leveraging MBZ meeting and FlyDubai incident

insights.claim: The Sept. 30 alleged hijacking attempt of a FlyDubai passenger plane could translate into additional support for Netanyahu.
insights.speaker: Mazal Mualem
insights.so_what: Security shocks feed a rally effect for the incumbent ahead of the vote.
insights.quote: the Sept. 30 alleged hijacking attempt of a FlyDubai passenger plane could translate into additional support for Netanyahu

insights.claim: The past week, including a meeting with MBZ, was an especially good one for Netanyahu as security took center stage in the campaign.
insights.speaker: Mazal Mualem
insights.so_what: High-profile Gulf diplomacy is being used as a campaign asset, signalling continued Israel-UAE engagement under Netanyahu.
insights.quote: The past week was an especially good one for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu
